text: Metropolitan Shio Mujiri - If we turn to the Lord for help, and if our desire is sincere and strong, He will surely come with His grace, correct us, and purify us.

"The Lord expects us to compel our wounded souls, burdened by sins, to turn to Him for salvation and mercy. Only God can bring about our correction and internal transformation; we are unable to do this by our own strength," stated the Locum Tenens of the Patriarchal Throne, Metropolitan Shio (Mujiri) of Senaki and Chkhorotsqu, during his sermon at the Holy Trinity Cathedral, where the Rite of the Deposition from the Cross was recently performed.
According to Metropolitan Shio, "if our desire is genuine, strong, and serious, the Lord will surely come with His grace, reform us, and purify us."

"Through the glorious and ancient divine services of our Church, composed by the great Holy Fathers, renowned hymnographers, the finest poets, thinkers, and sages, we are given the opportunity not only to learn of the events concerning the Lord Jesus Christ from the Gospel but, through these services, to become participants in those events. Therefore, today we have brought forth the Holy Shroud, and we are all participants in this event."

Those gathered here, we who are gathered, are not those who a short while ago were shouting – crucify Him, crucify Him, but rather those of us who say to the Lord – forgive us, Lord. We are instructed by the Church, we know the teaching of the Church, that through our sins we crucify the Lord again and again; He came to earth, became incarnate, suffered, and died in order to liberate us from the captivity of sin, from the burden of sins.

Who was the first person whom the Lord released from this burden? – One of the crucified thieves, the Wise Thief, who was so moved by the sufferings of the innocent Savior that he confessed his sins and turned to the Savior from the cross with repentance. This is exactly what the Lord expects from us: that we compel our wounded souls, burdened by our sins, to turn to God for salvation and mercy.

Many of us, some even for years, try independently to fix something in our souls and in our lives without God, relying on our own strength. This is a futile effort. It is merely a proud and foolish attempt, for only God can correct us and bring about internal change. We are unable to do this by our own power. We may slightly change our behavior externally, but it is impossible for us to change internally, just as the Lord says: "Without me, you can do nothing."

Dear brothers and sisters, the Lord desires our correction and purification. Let me remind you, once a sick man came to Him and said: "Lord, if You will, You can cleanse me." What did the Lord reply? – "I will; be cleansed." The Lord desires this. The will of man and God coincided, and that person was healed.

"So, the Lord desires our correction and purification even more than we do. If our desire is genuine, strong, and serious, and we turn to the Lord for help, He will surely come with His grace, correct us, and purify us. May God bless you and strengthen you. Let us pray to the Lord to give us strength and assistance to walk the path of truth and light, and together with Christ, amen," stated Metropolitan Shio.
